entities.label: Labyrinth
entities.blurb: Mark Pesce and Tony Parisi's scrappy 1994 prototype 3D web browser whose WWW94 demo willed VRML into existence.

entities.label: blaxxun Contact
entities.blurb: Black Sun/blaxxun's avatar-filled VRML community client, named straight out of Snow Crash's Black Sun bar.

entities.label: Live3D
entities.blurb: Paper Software's WebFX reborn as Netscape Live3D, the VRML plugin bundled straight into Navigator at the browser war's peak.

entities.label: WebSpace Navigator
entities.blurb: SGI and Template Graphics' Inventor-powered viewer, the first commercial VRML browser the world could actually run.

entities.label: WorldView

milestones.what: licensed to Microsoft for Internet Explorer

entities.blurb: Intervista's WorldView put VRML on ordinary Windows PCs and rode Internet Explorer to tens of millions of desktops.

entities.label: Sony Community Place

milestones.what: world's first VRML 2.0 browser released free
the SAPARi service closes in January

entities.blurb: Sony CSL's multi-user VRML 2.0 browser and server, filling shared worlds with avatars years before 'metaverse' was a pitch deck.

entities.label: Cosmo Player

milestones.what: sold with Cosmo Software to Platinum Technology, then CA

entities.blurb: SGI's polished VRML97 player, the de facto reference browser of the VRML era until corporate hand-offs orphaned it.

entities.label: FreeWRL
entities.blurb: The long-running open-source VRML/X3D browser that kept the standard runnable when the commercial players vanished.

entities.label: Cortona3D
entities.blurb: ParallelGraphics' Cortona plugin quietly inherited the VRML userbase after Cosmo's demise and pivoted into industrial 3D documentation.

entities.label: Vivaty (Media Machines / Flux)
entities.blurb: Tony Parisi's X3D-powered Flux player grown into Vivaty's in-browser virtual worlds, whose assets Microsoft picked up at shutdown.

entities.label: Unity Web Player

milestones.what: deprecated as browsers dropped NPAPI plugins

entities.blurb: The plugin that made real game engines routine inside browsers — until the plugin era itself was abolished.

entities.label: X3DOM
entities.blurb: Fraunhofer IGD's framework that dropped X3D scenes straight into the HTML DOM via WebGL — declarative 3D with no plugin at all.

entities.label: Sketchfab
entities.blurb: The YouTube of 3D models, which normalized embedding interactive 3D in any web page.

entities.label: Elation Engine
entities.blurb: Baicoianu's modular JavaScript game engine, the quiet foundation under JanusWeb's virtual worlds.

entities.label: JanusVR

milestones.what: company founded by McCrae and Singh in December
company folds; code released as open source

entities.blurb: The VR internet browser where webpages are rooms and links are portals, built by a Toronto team who open-sourced it all on the way out.

entities.label: FireBox
entities.blurb: James McCrae's 2014 experiment that treated web pages as rooms and hyperlinks as portals — the seed that became JanusVR.

entities.label: JanusWeb
entities.blurb: James Baicoianu's three.js-based engine that brought JanusVR's portal-linked rooms to any plain web browser, no install required.

entities.label: Mozilla Hubs

milestones.what: Mozilla shuts it down May 31; Hubs Foundation inherits the code

entities.blurb: Mozilla's open-source WebXR meeting rooms that ran in any browser and hosted nearly ten million visitors before the 2024 shutdown.

entities.label: JanusXR
entities.blurb: The community continuation of the Janus vision — an immersive, decentralized web of collaborative 3D spaces, kept alive by its ex-JanusVR builders.

entities.label: You are here
entities.blurb: This station. The line continues.
